title: Mockito unit tests
summary: Check real service decisions with controlled Mockito dependencies, without loading Spring.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Mockito Spring Boot Tutorial | @Mock @InjectMocks

richText: Mockito can supply a stand-in for one dependency while the class under test stays real.
A mock repository answers configured method calls. It does not query a database.
initializes Mockito support for a JUnit Jupiter test.
marks a field that Mockito creates as a mock.
asks Mockito to create the tested object and inject available mocks. Explicit constructor calls are also valid.
These Mockito annotations do not start Spring. They do not apply transactions, bean configuration, or Spring Security.
sets the value returned for a matching mock call. This setup is called stubbing.
checks that a call occurred. It does not call the real dependency.

example.title: Read a title without a database
description: Java `17` and Maven are required. The files form a separate project rooted at `pom.xml`.
`TitleRepository` is an ordinary Java interface for this example. It has no database implementation.
explanation: Mockito creates the repository mock before each test.
`@InjectMocks` calls the service constructor with that mock.
The first stub supplies a stored title. The second stub supplies an empty result.
The tests check the real service decisions for both cases.
The verification checks the requested ID. It does not prove a database query works.
